title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 335 (Certain attachments, executions, etc., in winding up by Tribunal to be void)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up by the Tribunal, any attachment, distress or execution put in force without leave of the Tribunal against the estate or effects of the company after the commencement of the winding up, and any sale of the company’s properties or effects held without such leave after commencement, shall be void. The section does not apply to proceedings for recovery of tax, impost or Government dues.
content.glance: Attachments, distress, executions and sales against the company after commencement of Tribunal winding up are void without Tribunal leave (except tax/Government recovery).
content.study: Section 335 preserves the Tribunal’s control over the company’s assets during a Tribunal winding up. After commencement, an attachment, distress or execution against the estate or effects of the company, or a sale of any of its properties or effects, is void if carried out without leave of the Tribunal. Sub-section (2) carves out proceedings for recovery of any tax or impost or any dues payable to the Government. The provision ensures that the liquidator, under Tribunal supervision, administers the estate free from competing enforcement actions.

sections.heading: Void enforcement without leave
sections.body: Attachment, distress, execution or sale after commencement of Tribunal winding up is void without Tribunal leave.

sections.heading: Government dues exception
sections.body: Proceedings for recovery of tax, impost or Government dues are not affected.

provisions.title: Certain attachments, executions, etc., in winding up by Tribunal to be void

examples.title: Execution without leave
examples.body: After a winding-up order, a decree-holder attaches and sells company machinery without Tribunal leave. The attachment and sale are void under s. 335.

hypotheticals.question: Can a tax authority recover arrears by attachment after commencement of Tribunal winding up?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 335(2) excludes proceedings for recovery of tax, impost or Government dues from the voidness rule.

misconceptions.trap: All post-commencement enforcement is void, including tax recovery.
misconceptions.correction: Tax, impost and Government dues recovery proceedings are expressly excluded by s. 335(2).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 335 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm Tribunal winding up and commencement. II. Identify the attachment/distress/execution/sale. III. Check leave of Tribunal and the Government-dues exception.

examTips: State the voidness rule and the tax/Government exception.
revisionPoints: Attachments/executions/sales after commencement void without leave
